title: Lotus Health AI vs FutureClinic: a free AI doctor, or a doctor-led visit
summary: Lotus Health AI vs FutureClinic compares a free California AI doctor with clinician sign-off to a $40 FutureClinic visit where a doctor reads your case.
body_markdown:
## How prices, incentives, and prescriptions compare


As of October 2026, Lotus Health AI is free and[requires no insurance](https://hlth.com/insights/news/lotus-health-ai-raises-35m-series-a-to-offer-free-insurance-free-doctor-visits-2026-02-05) , planning sponsor revenue. On FutureClinic, with no[subscription](https://futureclinic.com/blog/telehealth-subscriptions-vs-paying-a-doctor-per-visit-yearly-cost) required, pay $40 for the best-fit doctor or pick a doctor at their listed price, typically $20 to $100. Most doctors offer an optional membership, typically $25 to $100 a month (up to 100 responses monthly by law), for unlimited care with that doctor, cancel any time, and your visit fee counts toward joining.


FutureClinic sells no products, and your doctor earns nothing extra for any prescription or test. With no house formulary, your physician can prescribe any brand or generic medicine if your doctor decides it's right for you, with no subscription needed for refills. Prescriptions go to the pharmacy you choose, including mail-order pharmacies that deliver to your door, with a cash discount coupon and prior-authorization help when insurance needs one. Doctors can prescribe several months of a stable medicine when safe and order discounted labs (no controlled medicines).


## Who Lotus Health AI suits better, and what FutureClinic does instead


Lotus Health AI suits adults (18+) on iOS in California wanting free 24/7 AI chat in 50 languages, record and wearable aggregation, and clinician sign-off. Though February 2026 press noted 50-state licensing, Lotus's FAQ as of October 2026 says care is "only to patients who are physically located in the State of California." For a human physician writing your plan across 33 states and Washington, D.C., FutureClinic replies typically within a few hours, almost always the same day or the next, as real care takes hours, not seconds. On the US App Store as of October 26, 2026,[FutureClinic is rated 4.8 out of 5 from 40 ratings](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/futureclinic/id6747322849) , beside[Lotus Health AI at 4.4 out of 5 from 189 ratings](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/lotus-health-ai/id6736791154) .


Did you want a California-only iOS app where an AI drafts your care for a clinician to sign off on, or did you want a human physician of your own to read your case and write your plan? If you want Lotus Health AI's free 24/7 AI primary care app, it is a strong option, and if you wanted an expert doctor with nothing attached, FutureClinic is built for that.


## Messaging a FutureClinic physician across 33 states from your AI app


FutureClinic serves 33 states and Washington, D.C. with doctors licensed in your state: Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Montana, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, Wisconsin, Wyoming, and Washington, D.C. If you don't see your state, try anyway.


Lotus Health AI has no MCP server or AI-app access as of October 2026. FutureClinic works from[ChatGPT](https://futureclinic.com/blog/how-to-add-a-real-doctor-to-chatgpt) ,[Claude](https://futureclinic.com/blog/how-to-add-a-doctor-to-claude) , Claude Code, Codex, Grok Bot, Meta Muse, and Instinct, bringing your AI's context into intake. Start at[futureclinic.com/connect-your-ai](https://futureclinic.com/connect-your-ai) , or send your AI:


> ` Set up FutureClinic for me: read https://futureclinic.com/llms.txt`


Once it's connected, make sure you instruct your AI to use FutureClinic to help find you a doctor. Otherwise, it may not know that this is what you want.


Or visit[futureclinic.com](https://futureclinic.com/) and our[editorial standards](https://futureclinic.com/blog/editorial-standards) . FutureClinic is not for emergencies: call 911, or call or text 988 in a mental-health crisis.
